sections.title: If macOS does not start after a change
lines: In the OpenCore picker select macOS and press Shift+Enter: safe mode (-x). PG106, PG106FB, PG106Accel and the Wi-Fi kexts stand down there.
In safe mode open Helios 300 Setup and press Undo on the last step (or run helios-setup undo <step>), then restart.
If OpenCore itself does not come up: F12 at the Predator logo and pick the USB stick; its EFI is the known-good fallback.
After an update: Updates > Roll back last update (or helios-setup rollback) puts back the kexts and config.plist the update replaced.

sections.title: From Recovery (OpenCore picker > Space > Recovery > Utilities > Terminal)
lines: GPU kexts in /Library/Extensions: D=$(ls -d /Volumes/*Data | head -1); rm -rf "$D/Library/Extensions/PG106FB.kext" "$D/Library/Extensions/PG106Accel.kext" "$D/Library/KernelCollections/AuxiliaryKernelExtensions.kc"; reboot (macOS starts without the auxiliary collection and asks to rebuild it; other kexts in /Library/Extensions come back after that)
Internal EFI: diskutil mount disk0s1; the backups are /Volumes/EFI/EFI-backup-<date>/BOOT and /OC: copy them over /Volumes/EFI/EFI/BOOT and /EFI/OC

sections.title: Boot order
lines: If the Mac starts the stick, Windows or nothing after OpenCore was installed: firmware setup (F2 at the Predator logo) > Boot > Boot priority order, put the internal disk's EFI entry first (on a disk that had Windows it is named Windows Boot Manager), F10 saves.
F12 at the logo picks a boot device once (Main > F12 Boot Menu must be Enabled).
Status > Startup says whether this boot came from the internal disk or from the stick.

post_install.what: Install OpenCore to this Mac: EFI/BOOT and EFI/OC from the 1401 stick (or a release-built EFI folder) onto the internal disk's EFI partition, so the Mac starts without the stick. What was there is copied to EFI-backup-<date> on the same partition first; the new copy is staged, verified file by file against the source and only then swapped in; ocvalidate checks config.plist when one for the same OpenCore version is present. Done by Helios 300 Setup.app (or its helios-setup CLI)
needs: the 1401 stick's EFI folder (EFI/BOOT + EFI/OC) or a release-built one
free space on the internal EFI partition for the backup and the new copy
notes: If the Mac still starts from the stick (or Windows) after the restart: firmware setup (F2 at the Predator logo) > Boot > Boot priority order, put the internal disk's EFI entry first; F12 picks a boot device once
Undo puts the newest EFI-backup-<date> back (the EFI that was there is kept as EFI-backup-<date>-before-restore)

post_install.what: PG106FB.kext and PG106Accel.kext into /Library/Extensions (root:wheel 755, kmutil load -p, approve in System Settings if asked, restart): OpenCore cannot inject them, IOGraphicsFamily and IOAcceleratorFamily2 are only in the System KC on 26.7.2. Then the Metal plugin and nvmtl/ (NVK, translator) into /Library/GPUBundles with the plugin's per-app allow list. PG106FB attaches under PG106 once PG106Ready is Yes
post_install.cwd: the folder holding the release files and manifest.json (EFI/Helios300 on the stick, or a copy of it)
notes: If the Mac does not come up: Shift+Enter in the OpenCore picker (safe mode, -x): PG106, PG106FB and PG106Accel stand down; then MODE=revert

Which apps render on the GTX 1060: /Library/GPUBundles/nvmtl-allow.txt (one process name per line, an app's CFBundleExecutable; written only if none exists, system UI denied, no app allowed). One launch without a rule: NVMTL_ENABLE=1 /Applications/Foo.app/Contents/MacOS/Foo

gpu-apps.sh edits that list: bash gpu-apps.sh list; sudo bash gpu-apps.sh add /Applications/Foo.app (remove, deny the same way); bash gpu-apps.sh check Foo; bash gpu-apps.sh run [--log] /Applications/Foo.app (one launch on the GTX 1060). Changes apply to apps started afterwards
ONLY=PG106FB (then "plugin xlate nvk allow", then PG106Accel: the order of the driver's first-run playbook, nvidia-macos-driver tools/macos/README.md) installs one part per boot

post_install.what: Audio option 2 (recommended): AppleHDA 600.2 back on the root volume, step for step what OCLP 3.0.0's Modern Audio set does (PatcherSupportPkg 2.0.5 payload and KDK 25G332, both sha256-pinned). AppleALC layout 29 drives the ALC255 with its speaker EQ/limiter, NMHDA gives HDMI audio. The auxiliary collection (PG106FB, PG106Accel) is rebuilt for the new boot/system collections; VoodooHDA (option 1) is removed only after the new snapshot is blessed, so a stop before that leaves the machine as it was. Never let OCLP itself patch: it also wants the Nvidia Web Drivers, which would take the GTX 1060 from PG106
needs: 12 GiB free (14 when the KDK is downloaded)
network for the KDK (1.2 GB) unless cached
notes: MODE=dry-run changes nothing: it downloads and verifies the KDK into ~/Library/Caches/helios300-audio, mounts the payload read-only and test-builds the auxiliary collection
If PG106FB or PG106Accel is not loaded after the restart (MODE=status says so): MODE=aux, restart
Headset mic on the combo jack: test it; docs/HARDWARE.md 'Headset microphone' has the verbs if it is silent
HDMI audio appears with a monitor on HDMI (PG106FB modeset + ELD); never run on the laptop yet
A macOS update boots a new sealed snapshot without AppleHDA: bump the script's KDK pin to the new build, then run it again

Revert: MODE=revert boots the last sealed (Apple) snapshot and puts back its auxiliary collection; from Recovery: bless --mount "/Volumes/Macintosh HD" --bootefi --last-sealed-snapshot (full lines in docs/HARDWARE.md)

available.why_not: FileVault is on: turn it off (System Settings > Privacy & Security > FileVault) and wait until it has decrypted
pinned to macOS 25G332 (its KDK); this Mac runs another build: the script's KDK pin must be bumped first (a macOS update also removes AppleHDA: run it again after that)

detect.failed_hint: the patch record is on the booted system but AppleHDA is not loaded: Check (MODE=status) shows why; Undo boots Apple's sealed snapshot

post_install.what: Audio option 1 (fallback): VoodooHDA 3.6.8 into /Library/Extensions (sha256-pinned download) with a tuned Info.plist (TUNE=1: PCM 90, Rec 75, InhibitCache; TUNE=0 keeps the release's). Reversible, no root-volume change; speakers, headphones and microphones through the ALC255; no speaker EQ and NO HDMI audio
notes: Use it only if option 2 cannot be used: it sounds worse (no speaker processing)
No HDMI audio: VoodooHDA does not match the GP106's 10de:10f1 and NMHDA needs AppleHDA
Other levels: VHDA_PCM=85 VHDA_REC=60 MODE=install (docs/HARDWARE.md 'Option 1 sound'); each change needs a restart
If headphones or the microphone stay silent with the BIOS pins: NODES=1 MODE=install (ALC255 pin fallback)
Survives macOS updates (nothing on the root volume)

post_install.what: Allow sleep again: sudo pmset -a disablesleep 0 (undo: disablesleep 1). Sleep stays disabled until the GTX 1060 driver's sleep/wake has passed checklist (a) of nvidia-macos-driver tools/macos/README.md on this Mac; turn it on for that test, or once it has passed
notes: With boot-arg pg106_pm=0 PG106 has no power management and the Mac must not sleep: the step is not available then
A black screen that never wakes: hard reset, boot with pg106_pm=0, report (driver README checklist (a))
